state:
Product: Kenmore 4 Burner Gas Grill Model # 720-0830A (category: Gas or Lp Grills or Stoves (For Outdoor Use))
Incident description: On April 18, 2014 I purchased a gas grill from Sear's store located in Seaford Delaware a Kenmore Model# 720-0830A. I used my grill over the next few weeks and had intermittent problems getting it to light. Sometimes it would light on the first attempt like you would normally expect and other times it took several attempts to get it to light. On July 8, 2014 I attempted to light the grill at approximately 1850 hours. My first few attempts to get the grill lit were unsuccessful. I tried several different burners thinking there may be a problem with one or two specific burners. I then took the regulator off of the LP gas tank, I remove the tank to feel it's weight. After verifying the tank was heavy and had plenty of fuel I reattach the regulator and install the tank in the grill. I again attempted to light the grill and was unsuccessful. I turned on several burners in an attempt to get fuel to the burners. When I pressed the igniter a large ball of fire came out of the top of the grill (which was open) as well as the bottom of the grill (where the gas tank is stored). I was blown back a bit. Once I stood up I found I had sustained burns to my left leg, left arm, neck and face. I was immediately taken to the emergency department at my local hospital. From there I was transferred within the hour to a specialty burn care hospital in Baltimore, Johns Hopkins Bayview Hospital. I spent the next two days in the burn intensive care unit. I had sustained second-degree burns over 6% of my body. After being discharged and recovering for the next few weeks I again attempted to use the grill. My first attempt at using the grill after my recovery was successful. The grill lit just as anticipated and had no problems. My second attempt at using the grill was unsuccessful and I again could not get it lit after multiple attempts using multiple different burners. After being frustrated from spending $400 on a grill that I could never longer use I started looking for remedies. I was strongly suspicious of the gas regulator being faulty. My reason for the suspicion was the fact that at times when lighting it you could not even smell gas. I felt as though the regulator would not always pass fuel. I purchased a new gas regulator and hose I installed it on the grill and I've now been using it for several weeks with no issues at all. I strongly suspect the gas regulator has some type of defect. I contacted Sears and was transferred around amongst many departments finally landing in the recall department. I spoke to a gentleman and told him my story I gave him the model number of my grill he responded with "yes your grill has a recall". The gentleman stated that parts would be sent out to my home and once I receive them to call the numbers provided and a technician would come out and replace the faulty parts. I asked him to elaborate on the recall because I wanted to know if it was safe to use or what parts were involved in the recall. He stated he only had part numbers and had no further information, he then transferred me to the service department. I spoke to a very nice gentleman there that put the model number into the computer and then told me there was no recall and had no idea with the other gentleman was talking about. He did suggest that I contact the Consumer Product Safety Commission and file a report. I simply don't want this to happen to anyone else. I have retained the original gas regulator should your agency want it for testing purposes. I would be happy to answer any questions or provide additional documentation such as receipt for the grill, medical records, and pictures of my injuries. Thank you for your time and looking into this matter.

state:
Product: Laundry Detergent (category: Laundry Soaps or Detergents)
Incident description: The caller is a Medical Director at the California Poison Control System. 

He says the product is brightly packaged and they look like candy. It is wrapped in a plastic film. Children pick this product up, which is the size of a golf ball and bite into it. He says they are very attractively colored, inviting, and are getting children really sick.

The caller says this has been happening mostly since March 7th. He has seen incidents of 139 children get into these products since that time. Almost all of them are 3 years of age and under. Five have been admitted to hospitals. Three to critical care units. 

9 of these kids have had moderate affects and one major affect according to the Poison Control Centers codes. 

The children have experienced significant vomiting and nausea. Secondly, is respiratory distress. 

Thirdly is Lactic Acidosis and eye injuries. When children open the pods with their teeth, the substance sometimes gets in there eyes. 

The caller feels that 139 exposures in 3 1/2 months is troubling. Lactic Acidosis is a risk that they don't understand why it is occurring but it doesn't usually stem from getting into laundry detergent. 

The caller feels CPSC should step in and require more labeling and also the way that it is packaged differently to not be so inviting for children.

Incident description: Per police reports, on September 26, 2021, about 1000-1015 hours, the baby was given to his father and placed in an Ergo baby carrier. The baby was positioned facing his father. The father reportedly took the baby and their dog for a walk around the neighborhood. The baby's head, arms, legs, and feet were exposed. At some point, the head cover was placed over the infant's head. The father returned home between 1045-1100 hours and prepared to go out for the afternoon. He kept the baby in the carrier with him. At about 1200 hours, the father and mother left the home to take the baby and their sibling to the park. As the father went to remove the baby from the carrier, he noticed the baby was not moving. He took the baby to the mother who also observed the baby did not look right. When the parents tried to wake the baby up, they noticed blood coming from his nose. The mother called 911 and initiated CPR. EMS arrived on the scene and continued life-saving efforts. The baby was transported to Children's hospital for advance care but despite all efforts, the decedent was pronounced dead at 1300 hours.

Product: POCKET HOSE, made in China, sold on TV and by TARGET Bar code 0 97298 02296 8. Sold by TARGET for. (category: Garden Hoses, Nozzles or Sprinklers)
Incident description: My 9 year old granddaughter, while using the hose to water plants, was struck violently by the hose on her upper
left arm when the hose separated at its terminal end at the junction with the plastic threaded connector (See
photos). The action was so violent that the severed end or the threaded connector cut the skin in two places and
caused whelps and bruises on the skin in 5 places (See photos). She was using the hose normally under my
supervision at the time. She immediately screamed in pain. As she refused to move her arm and concerned about a
sprain or torn ligament, I called her father, a physician, requesting he observe her injuries. He purchased pain
medication in child dosage strength and gave it to her. He also recommended ice packs and a topical anti-bacterial
ointment with pain relief ingredients.
The hose was being used as intended and normal for a water hose. Our water service is provided by a municipal
water supply, not self regulated by a private well. Our water pressure is considered good or very good, but not
unsafe. The hose had been stored loosely coiled on the porch in the shade immediately prior to use.
Any reasonable person, after reviewing the facts of this incident, would be concerned about similar injuries or the
real potential for eye injury if the hose was used at or above face level, as is done while watering hanging baskets or
washing windows. To quate my granddaughter, "They should stop selling those things!".

state:
Product: POCKET HOSE, made in China, sold on TV and by TARGET Bar code 0 97298 02296 8. Sold by TARGET for. (category: Garden Hoses, Nozzles or Sprinklers)
Incident description: My 9 year old granddaughter, while using the hose to water plants, was struck violently by the hose on her upper
left arm when the hose separated at its terminal end at the junction with the plastic threaded connector (See
photos). The action was so violent that the severed end or the threaded connector cut the skin in two places and
caused whelps and bruises on the skin in 5 places (See photos). She was using the hose normally under my
supervision at the time. She immediately screamed in pain. As she refused to move her arm and concerned about a
sprain or torn ligament, I called her father, a physician, requesting he observe her injuries. He purchased pain
medication in child dosage strength and gave it to her. He also recommended ice packs and a topical anti-bacterial
ointment with pain relief ingredients.
The hose was being used as intended and normal for a water hose. Our water service is provided by a municipal
water supply, not self regulated by a private well. Our water pressure is considered good or very good, but not
unsafe. The hose had been stored loosely coiled on the porch in the shade immediately prior to use.
Any reasonable person, after reviewing the facts of this incident, would be concerned about similar injuries or the
real potential for eye injury if the hose was used at or above face level, as is done while watering hanging baskets or
washing windows. To quate my granddaughter, "They should stop selling those things!".

state:
Product: Sylvania-Zinsco power Panel: MLB20(20-40)C Indoor Mod 1, 225 Amps Max. 120/240 VAC 1 phase - 3 wire. 120/208 VAC 3W WYE. (category: Panelboards, Circuit Breakers, Gfci"s, or Fuses)
Incident description: When my 6 month old water heater stopped working, I checked my Sylvania-Zinsco breaker panel for a tripped circuit breaker. Seeing none tripped, I looked for the circuit breaker identified as Water Heater (double pole, 30A). The breaker was not tripped. I moved the breaker handles from ON to OFF, at which time I noted that the bottom one of the two (not-connected handles) did not snap all the way off; instead, I could move it to the OFF position, but it would move back to approximately 1/8" shy of the OFF position. I acquired a new breaker and when the old one was removed, I saw there is a charred/burned hole in the plastic housing of the breaker on the same side/pole that would not move to the OFF position.

Neither hot wire appeared to be burned.

After replacement of this breaker with a Connecticut Electric UBIZ-0230 Zinsco Circuit Breaker 2 Pole 30 Amp, the water heater was restored to operation.

Now, however, I suspect all the other breakers in this panel; especially after reading about the failure of other similar panels. My Sylvania panel number is MLB20(20-40)C Indoor Mod 1, 225 Amp Max. 120/240 VAC 1phase - 3 wire. 120/208 VAC SW WYE.

state:
Heading: Question about mounting hard disks on Fedora 17
After I had upgraded to Fedora 17, I found that when I first booted it up, everything worked, but when I shut the computer down and booted it up again, Fedora went to emergency mode before I could even log in, asking me for the root password, and when I gave it, dropped me to a text-only shell. In panic that I had broken the system, I reinstalled Fedora 17 and everything worked, but after I rebooted, the same problem appeared again.
I decided to google "Fedora emergency mode" and found the cause of the problem. I have additional Lacie external hard drives that I use for back-up, but I keep them powered down when they're not in use. I have written entries for them in /etc/fstab so that I can manually mount and unmount them with a single command. Now what was happening was that on boot-up, Fedora found these entries in /etc/fstab and tried to mount them, but failed because the disks were powered off. This caused Fedora to think "Oh no! Mounting file systems has failed! Let's stop right here and inform the user that something has gone horribly wrong!", which I took as a corrupted system.
Is there any way to write the entries to /etc/fstab telling the computer that the drives should not be mounted on boot-up, they'll be mounted when I say so? |

Heading: Why does sticking your thumb on a water hose make the water come out faster?
I'm not sure if this is the right place to ask this question, but our article on the List of common misconceptions states (depending on which edit you happen to look at):
It is not true that a nozzle (or a person's thumb) on the end of a garden hose makes the water squirt farther because the same amount of water gets forced through a smaller opening. The rate of flow of water through the hose is not a set constant; in fact, putting one's thumb over the end of the hose reduces the rate of flow. What is constant is the water pressure at the source. When water is flowing, the pressure decreases the farther from the source one gets due to friction between the water and the pipes it's flowing through. The faster the water moves through the pipe, the greater is the friction that cuts down pressure at the output end. A thumb over the end of the hose decreases the flow rate, causing the friction from the source to decrease, causing the remaining water to have more speed. 
A discussion is here 
Would some editors who know more about friction and pressure help settle this issue?

Heading: Why does sticking your thumb on a water hose make the water come out faster?
I'm not sure if this is the right place to ask this question, but our article on the List of common misconceptions states (depending on which edit you happen to look at):
It is not true that a nozzle (or a person's thumb) on the end of a garden hose makes the water squirt farther because the same amount of water gets forced through a smaller opening. The rate of flow of water through the hose is not a set constant; in fact, putting one's thumb over the end of the hose reduces the rate of flow. What is constant is the water pressure at the source. When water is flowing, the pressure decreases the farther from the source one gets due to friction between the water and the pipes it's flowing through. The faster the water moves through the pipe, the greater is the friction that cuts down pressure at the output end. A thumb over the end of the hose decreases the flow rate, causing the friction from the source to decrease, causing the remaining water to have more speed. 
A discussion is here 
Would some editors who know more about friction and pressure help settle this issue?
